name: The Open Plain
_comment: The open area, rebuilt as real geometry. There is no panorama any more:
a backdrop is only correct from the single point it was rendered from, so
it held the player inside a 26x52m box while the gate it showed stayed
exactly as far away however long they walked. Everything here is now a
real model on a real plain, and the only thing you cannot walk through is
Site positions are laid out so no two are in line from the spawn point -
each one has to be walked to, and walking to one puts another in view.

spawn._comment: East of the ruined city, on the ground the road to the sacred place will run over, facing west into the ruins. It was at (0,-52), which put arrivals inside the shrine - and once the ruins had colliders that stopped being a cosmetic problem and started being a cell.

ground._comment: The pack's own desert terrain, run to the edges of the 2400m plane so the sand does not stop before the mountains do.

sky._comment: Trying the free sci-fi panorama. 2048x1024 equirectangular - half the resolution of the desert sky it replaces, and it carries a painted landscape in its lower half that has to sit behind our real dunes.

sites._comment: Thirty-four kit pieces laid out as one city: shrine and altar at the centre, a colonnade in from the south where players spawn, buildings scattered off-square, walls fragmenting outward and rubble half-buried at the edges. See art/build_ruins.py.

Nine buildings assembled from the EmbersStorm Mediterranean kit and standing east of the desert ruin, about a minute's walk away. The kit ships no composed scene - its demo scene is a parts catalogue, each of the 92 modules laid out once in rows - so these are authored in art/build_village.py. Positions are baked into the glb, hence 0,0 here.

Twenty-four structures from Stein's Ruins Ancient City, scattered across the plain around the desert city so the horizon keeps offering another broken wall. Each decimated from up to 40k triangles to 3k - they are read as silhouettes across sand. Positions baked into the glb, hence 0,0.

The Sacred Place Universe kit, composed here - the pack ships parts and a demo scene holding only animated cloud effects, which are a Unity shader and do not travel. A raised platform at (165,0), ringed with twelve columns, arch facing the ruins, sphere over the centre. Symmetrical and intact where the ruins are scattered and broken: they are where people have been, this is where they go.

Stones from the ruin pack pressed into the sand between the city and the sacred platform. Two edge rows and a scatter between, wandering slightly - a path laid straight across open ground looks surveyed.

The ruins level, organised into districts so a search is navigable: a necropolis north-west, a ring of standing stones north, a colonnade east pointing at the sacred place, overgrown ruins south-west, and 8m archway pillars scattered as beacons so no direction is featureless. A player who cannot tell one stretch of broken wall from another cannot remember where they have already looked.
A carved relief on the shrine wall, facing the road in from the east. Decimated 457,514 triangles to 8,000 - it was a sculpt export priced for a close-up.

_sites_comment: The five sacred monuments are parked, not deleted - the playable area is the Ancient Desert Ruin pack for now, to see what that aesthetic gives. Restore by moving sites_parked back to sites.

move._comment: Metres per second, matched to the clips in remy.glb: the walk covers 1.16 m/s and the run 3.44, so both play near 1x and the feet do not skate. Backwards and sideways are scaled down in Walker.update to suit their own clips.

horizon._comment: No ring. Six decimated alpine tiles standing at 620m read as grey lumps no matter how they were lit or textured - snowy peaks around a desert was the wrong idea before it was a bad execution. The sky closes the horizon on its own until dunes replace it.
